newsitem.title: UK: Northern Irish police arrest one over IRA bombing.
newsitem.headline: Northern Irish police arrest one over IRA bombing.

text.p: Police investigating the IRA bombing of Britain's army headquarter in Northern Ireland said on Thursday they had arrested a man.
Thirty-one people were injured in the double car bomb attack on the garrison in Lisburn, 10 miles (15 km) from Belfast on Monday. Police called it "a deliberate attempt at mass murder".
The IRA (Irish Republican Army), fighting to end British rule in Northern Ireland, has admitted to setting off the two car bombs, each with 500 pounds (225 kg) of explosives, inside the army base.
"Early this morning, a male from the Belfast area was arrested," a police spokesman said. He said the man was being questioned but gave no further details.

The bombing was the IRA's first attack in Northern Ireland in more than two years. The guerrilla group ended a 17-month ceasefire on February 9 with the first of a series of attacks on the British mainland.
The arrest came less than 24 hours after police issued a photofit picture of one of the suspected Lisburn bombers, apparently heavily disguised in a hood, beard and dark glasses.
